text:
maya: thinking we should build a small 'release cookbook' CLI that wraps common deploy-bot flows + auto-generates release notes. small RFC idea, not a full overhaul.
chris: yes please. last week there was a lot of copy/paste in release notes.
liam: curious — what would the CLI do vs just adding more bot commands?
maya: good q. my mental model:
- a few opinionated templates (canary, full-prod, hotfix)
- validate preflight (schema + smoke tests) before invoking deploy-bot
- generate changelog from PR labels + changelog fragments
- attach suggested rollback steps to the release note
- expose a dry-run mode that outputs the exact /deploy command

jen: love the rollback suggestions idea. ops always asks for an explicit rollback plan.
sophia: can we make templates live in a git repo? e.g. infra/release-cookbook/templates so teams can add custom ones.
chris: +1 to templates in git. also make the CLI idempotent and safe for CI.
liam: timeline? I can prototype a minimal PoC if we agree on an interface.
maya: prototype scope:
- CLI: rwd-release (python) with commands: init, plan, run, rollback
- store templates in YAML; basic schema: name, steps, preflight, canary-config
- plan -> prints deploy-bot invocation + release notes draft
- run -> posts to deploy-bot (via webhook) or prints command in dry-run

maya: example usage (mock):
```
# draft a canary release and open changelog PR
rwd-release plan --template canary-quick --branch release/2026-03-22 --changelog auto

# actually execute (will call deploy-bot)
rwd-release run --template canary-quick --commit abc123 --change-window "2026-03-22T02:00Z/2h"
```

deploy-bot: @maya Started deploy run 8142 (canary-quick) — status: queued. Preflight checks pending.
chris: for preflight checks we should require: lint, unit tests, infra-sanity (smoke), model-compat checks for serving changes.
liam: can the CLI show estimated cost/latency delta? even a rough delta would help product decide canary size.
maya: yes — we can integrate a small estimator that reads model profile + canary weight and outputs token/s cost estimate.
jen: release notes auto-gen rules?
sophia: use PR labels: feat/fix/docs; include changelog fragment if present; fall back to PR title + summary.
chris: also add a `sensitive: true` flag for templates so the CLI prompts for approvals and disables auto-publish.
liam: for rollback, let's include a machine-readable rollback snippet in the release note, like:
```
# rollback plan
rwd-release rollback --run-id 8142 --strategy immediate
```
jen: can the CLI suggest the rollback command automatically based on the template? that would be super helpful in incidents.
maya: yes, we'll store rollback mappings in template YAMLs. also include a quick way to generate an incident-playbook link.

sophia: one operational caveat: deploy-bot rate limits. if CLI becomes popular we might need a batching or job queue to avoid thundering herd.
chris: agree. maybe CLI pushes a job into a service that the deploy-bot reads, rather than calling bot webhooks directly.

liam: PoC offer: I can wire `rwd-release plan` to output deploy-bot command and generated markdown for release notes. can demo next Wed.
maya: perfect. next steps:
1) liam PoC for plan + dry-run (due Wed)
2) create infra/release-cookbook repo + two starter templates (canary, hotfix)
3) make a deploy-bot endpoint for job queueing (eng-infra)
4) add estimator prototype (optional for PoC)

jen: sounds great. add me as reviewer on the repo when created.
sophia: tagging privacy/security: please include checklist for secrets and KMS keys in preflight.
chris: I'll sketch a minimal YAML schema for templates and paste here tomorrow.
maya: thanks all. small ask: put short feedback in the RFC doc I just shared: https://rwd.internal/s/rel-cookbook
:thumbsup:
